Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message to Barcelona as the countdown continues towards his return to Manchester United.

Rashford spent last season on loan at the Nou Camp, contributing 14 goals and 14 assists as the Catalans won La Liga and reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

However, Barca decided not to trigger an option to buy him from United for £26million before a deadline in mid-June, and signed Newcastle’s Anthony Gordon for £70m.

On Thursday, Rashford posted a picture on social media of his No.14 shirt and another of him in action for the club with the message: ‘I am extremely grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here a positive and unforgettable experience. I enjoyed every moment, and I will keep many special memories. I wish the club and all its fans every success in the coming season. Visca Barca!’

Rashford is now set to rejoin United where he has a contract until June 2028 worth around £315,000-a-week. The England international is having some time off after helping England reach the World Cup semi-finals, and it remains to be seen if he will be involved in United’s training camp in Ireland next month which includes a friendly against Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

With United in need of a left-sided attacker, and Rashford contracted to his boyhood club for another two seasons, it makes sense for the 28-year-old to come back and play under head coach Michael Carrick.

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message following his season long loan at Barcelona

It is looking increasingly like Rashford will be at Man United when the transfer window closes

There is no chance of a repeat of last summer when the more confrontational Ruben Amorim placed him in a ‘bomb squad’ of five players who trained separately from the main group at Carrington before Rashford left for Barcelona.

After initially putting a price of £40m on their top-earner this summer in the hope of moving him off the wage bill, it has been difficult for United to find a club willing to pay more than the £26m stipulated in the Barca loan as well as Rashford’s salary.

The club also discovered the high cost of replacing him when one option, West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, joined Al-Hilal for £60m.

There is still time for some twists and turns before the window closes on September 1, but it’s looking increasingly likely that Rashford will be at United when it does.

Sports.title: Chaos at the Commonwealth Games as HUGE crash in wheelchair race forces organisers to order a re-run as England star is left 'traumatised' at thought of losing medal
Sports.content:
Chaos at the Commonwealth Games as HUGE crash in wheelchair race forces organisers to order a re-run as England star is left 'traumatised' at thought of losing medal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England’s Ellis Kottas was left ‘lowkey traumatised’ at the prospect of losing her silver medal after Commonwealth chiefs ordered a re-race following a mass wheelchair crash.

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification.

Scotland’s Melanie Woods finished first with Commonwealth record of 3min 33.39sec but the athletes were told the following morning that they must race again.

Kottas said: ‘While I’m lowkey traumatised if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit, so I will go out and give it all I’ve got. If I don’t medal so be it, I’ll still have the incredible memories of lifting that England flag.'

The decision was criticised by Team England’s chef de mission, Jonny Riall, who said: ‘We are incredibly disappointed by the late decision. While there is no formal protest process available to us, we have strongly challenged the decision.

A huge crash out on the first bend of the women's 1500m T54 final 😬 pic.twitter.com/wWNxhKIGqb — TNT Sports (@tntsports) July 29, 2026

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification

'While I really don’t want to rerun the race (lowkey traumatised) if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit,' silver medallist Ellis Kottas said

'The race officials did not halt the race at the time of the incident, nor was any immediate decision made to declare the race void or order a rerun.

'Our priority is the welfare of our athletes. We will now do everything we can do support Ellis during the extremely short turnaround.'

Compliments to the chef as Emily reigns supreme

Not since the Finnieston Crane was in action have Glasgow’s docklands witnessed such large masses of metal being thrown around.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift.

On the banks of the River Clyde, England’s Olympian showed her adoring fans why she is regarded as the sport’s great entertainer.

She blew kisses to the crowd and told her rivals that there is ‘life in this old bird yet’ before collecting her medal from the Duchess of Edinburgh.

It takes thousands of calories to fuel a weightlifter and next month Campbell will continue to fly the flag for her sport when the takes part in Celebrity MasterChef.

‘MasterChef is definitely more nerve-racking!’ she laughed.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift

‘It’s really nice for me to do something without being Emily the weightlifter, to just do something as Emily. My signature dish is Caribbean and that’s all I’m going to give you because I want you to watch it! It’s another platform to put weightlifting in, another time for us to have that spotlight on us.

At 32, the weightlifting game is beginning taking its toll on her joints. Olympic gold still eludes her but she is yet to commit to competing at LA 2028.

‘We’ve got to look at the practicalities of LA,’ she said. ‘We have to do a slightly different qualification process to other sports. We’ve got to look at that and we can get our body through.

'If I go to LA, I would want to be in contention for a medal, so we want to make sure that that’s feasible. We just have to be very sensible about decisions and hopefully you’ll see me there.

'But for now, we enjoy what happened. We have some good food, maybe a few drinks. We're out in Glasgow!'

Sports.title: John Stones seals Inter Milan move, Brentford close in on £41m deal for Mamadou Sangare... and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage as they also offer £1.8m for Marseille keeper: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City bid £1.8m for goalkeeper Rulli

Manchester City have made an offer of around £1.8million for Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli.

The 34-year-old Argentine was previously signed by City in 2016 but was sent out on loan.

He has been offered a two-year contract if Marseille accept City's offer.

Stones seals Inter switch

Inter Milan have confirmed the signing of England defender John Stones.

The 32-year-old left Inter's headquarters earlier this evening after having his medical and agreeing a two-year contract after his free transfer from Manchester City.

Inter Milan have confirmed the signing of England defender John Stones

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026

Meanwhile, talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60million before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford and have offered Marseille's Geronimo Rulli a two-year deal. They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that the teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now, though the French club would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

Brighton's Espi move falls through

Brighton's proposed move for Levante striker Carlos Espi has collapsed after Real Madrid surprisingly agreed to sign the 21-year-old centre forward.

Espi scored 11 goals last season and narrowly missed out on a place in Spain’s World Cup squad, and he has been brought in to replace Fulham-bound Gonzalo Garcia.

The youngster had a number of Premier League enquiries, with Brighton seeing him as replacement for Danny Welbeck, until Real swooped.

Better Latte than never for Union Berlin as Boro thwarted by visa rules

Middlesbrough and Burnley are poised to miss out on signing Emmanuel Latte Lath as he closes on a move to Union Berlin.

The Ivory Coast international left Boro in 2025 for Atlanta United but wants to leave the Major League Soccer after a disappointing spell.

Middlesbrough had tried for an initial loan but the 27-year-old did not have enough points to earn a UK visa. Now Union Berlin are discussing a deal.

Emmanuel Latte Lath played for Boro from 2023 to 2025 but visa rules ruled him out of a return

From Benfica to Bournemouth for £21.6m

Benfica defender Antonio Silva is expected to complete his move to Bournemouth following tonight's Europa League qualifier against St Gallen.

The 22-year-old starts for Marco Silva's side against the Swiss tonight but is then due to link up with his new teammates at Bournemouth in a £21.6million move.

Newcastle close in on Hornicek

Newcastle United are pressing ahead with their move for Sporting Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Newcastle's interest last weekend and he was left out of Braga's Europa Conference League squad for tonight's clash with Zeleznicar Pancevo amid talks.

Confirmation of the Czech keeper's departure for his £25m release clause is expected tomorrow once their game is out of the way.

Brentford set for £41m Sangare deal

Brentford have agreed a £41million deal to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare.

The 24-year-old is preparing to travel to the UK for a medical after a meeting with club officials in Paris.

A sell-on is due to be included also while his former club Rapid Wien are also due a percentage.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday evening how Brentford had stepped up their interest to sign the Mali international as it became apparent they would be agreeing to mutually terminate Jordan Henderson's contract and pave the way for him to join Chelsea.

Brentford had a long-held interest in Sangare but had to fend off competition from two other English clubs including Crystal Palace.

Wednesday's Daily Mail carried news of Brentford's move for Sangare

Foxes eye Brighton winger Watson

Leicester City have enquired about taking Brighton winger Tommy Watson on loan.

The 20-year-old, who was key to Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League 18 months ago, had a spell on loan at Millwall last season.

Tommy Watson helped secure Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League via the playoffs

Porto keep tabs on Spurs man Souza

Porto are the latest team to show interest in Tottenham left wing-back Souza.

The 21-year-old joined from Santos for £13m in January and made four Premier League appearances last season.

Hail Cesar as Fulham get their man from Madrid

Fulham have agreed to buy 22-year-old forward Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid for £35million. The deal is of a similar structure to the £8.5m one they have agreed for his team-mate, midfielder Cesar Palacios, with Madrid retaining a 30 per cent sell-on clause and matching rights.

Fulham, now managed by former Real boss Alvaro Arbeloa, are also among clubs interested in Arsenal’s Ethan Nwaneri and Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Nwaneri also has interest from RB Leipzig and AC Milan.

Cesar Palacios has been secured for a fee of £8.5million

Fredricson moves on

Manchester United defender Tyler Fredricson has agreed a permanent move to Swiss club Lausanne-Sport, subject to registration.

Fredricson made four first-team appearances since he was handed a debut against Wolves in 2025 – when he also won the reserve-team player of the year award – and was on the bench on a number of occasions last season.

United have inserted a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back clause into the deal.

The 21-year-old, who joined United at Under-9 level, played in every round of United’s successful FA Youth Cup campaign in 2022 until illness ruled him out of the final against Nottingham Forest.

The club confirmed Fredricson’s departure in a statement on Thursday, saying: ‘Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.’

Fredricson joins United loanee Sekou Kone at the Swiss Super League side.

CHRIS WHEELER

Rashford says no to Roma

Marcus Rashford has no interest in joining Roma this summer as speculation regarding his future grows.

The 28-year-old is set to report to pre-season training with Manchester United in the coming days after returning from his loan spell with Barcelona.

Roma had been one of several clubs linked with a move for the England attacker, but Daily Mail Sport understands a move to the Italian giants does not appeal.

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal worth £35m for striker Gonzalo Garcia. The deal also includes £2m in bonuses and matching rights.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a 30 per cent sell-on clause as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

Coventry explore Hamer homecoming

Coventry City are exploring a deal to re-sign Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United.

The 29-year-old midfielder has one year left on his deal at Bramall Lane.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Sports.title: Game over Gianni! As deplorable megalomaniac Infantino's grand plan to sell off the World Cup goes up in smoke, DAILY MAIL SPORT tells the humiliated FIFA president he must RESIGN
Sports.content:
As every megalomaniac finds out in the end, there comes a point in the power trip when the writing is on the wall.

For the deplorable Gianni Infantino, that moment arrived after UEFA’s 55 member associations made it clear they will not stand for FIFA’s plot to sell off the World Cup to the highest bidders.

UEFA will boycott FIFA competitions – including the World Cup itself – unless these preposterous plans are consigned to the dustbin where they belong. Concacaf were next to show their displeasure, with their 41 members also rejecting Infantino's plan.

Quite right. But it shouldn’t end there. How can Infantino stay in office when he has betrayed the sport he has been trusted to lead and plunged FIFA into all-out war with UEFA, the biggest federation in world football?

The 56-year-old has declared his intention to stand for re-election as FIFA president at the next congress in Morocco in March 2027. If he had any shred of dignity, Infantino would get out long before football has the chance to kick him out.

Go, Gianni, go!

If Gianni Infantino had a shred of dignity the FIFA president would get out long before football has the chance to kick him out, after his plans to sell off the World Cup were opposed

UEFA's 55 members, including newly crowned world champions Spain, vowed to boycott the World Cup should FIFA's plans go ahead

UEFA, led by Aleksander Ceferin, issued a blistering statement declaring that the World Cup 'is not for sale' and accused Infantino of presiding over 'governance by intimidation'

Like so many of the club executives who hatched the doomed European Super League in secret back in 2021 only to see it go up in flames on the launch-pad, Infantino should do the decent thing and quit now that it’s clear his clandestine plans to raise £3.1billion in private investment are in tatters too.

‘The World Cup is not for sale,’ declared a blistering statement from UEFA, agreed unanimously and co-signed by the English FA and Europe’s other 54 associations. They criticised Infantino for ‘a profound failure of leadership’ and presiding over ‘governance by intimidation’.

They described his attempts to flog the family silver behind their backs without any consultation whatsoever as both ‘irresponsible’ and ‘indefensible’.

The man who sold out to co-hosts USA this summer with the commercially driven hydration breaks, ridiculously long half-time show during the final between Spain and Argentina, and the unforgivable decision to suspend Folarin Balogun’s red card at the behest of his buddy, President Donald Trump, so the striker could play in the last 16 against Belgium, has now hit a major roadblock in his efforts to sell off the World Cup itself.

Even Sepp Blatter, Infantino’s predecessor and another FIFA despot who hails from the Valais region of Switzerland, has branded the plan as ‘deeply damaging’ to the game.

When you have gone too far even for a man like Blatter, you must know that your moral compass is off.

Like Blatter, Infantino is likely to ignore our plea to leave and fight on for his long as he can and bank on the support of the smaller federations in his battle against UEFA, possibly right up to next year’s congress.

For the sake of football’s future, we can only hope he fails.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino in trouble as new statement released after UEFA fury over World Cup plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino in trouble as new statement released after UEFA fury over World Cup plans

FIFA's controversial plans that would affect the World Cup have been met with anger from the football community, with CONCACAF joining UEFA in issuing a statement

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plans have been slammed (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

CONCACAF have rejected Gianni Infantino's plans to sell parts of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. Their opposition to the plan proceeds UEFA's statement which pledged to boycott all FIFA competitions until the idea was dead in the water.

‌



Earlier this week, plans emerged that saw FIFA announce their intention to sell shares in its competitions, including the World Cup, which just took place in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Leading organisations within the sport have criticised the plans, with the FA supporting a recent statement issued by UEFA.

‌



After UEFA held a meeting in response to controversial proposals put forward by FIFA president Gianni Infantino that would see private investment introduced, CONCACAF, which makes up the nations in North and Central America including the USA and Canada, also converged their member nations to discuss the pitch.

‌



Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot READ MORE :

UEFA statement in FULL as they boycott World Cup until FIFA abandon controversial proposal READ MORE :

They outlined their position in a statement which read: "Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organization founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

"History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values. With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish ‘FIFA Forward Enterprise’ and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors.

"During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned. The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing vast FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes. Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future—and its greatest asset—must remain in the hands of our football family."

UEFA released their own statement in response to the controversial plans, making their position clear that they will not participate in FIFA competitions as long as the proposals remain in play. The statement read: “UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

‌



“The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plans have been met with fury by UEFA members (Image: AFP or licensors)

“It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

‌



“National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process.

“The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

“This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

‌



“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

“Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

Article continues below

“Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola handed Liverpool setback as injury blow confirmed
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola handed Liverpool setback as injury blow confirmed

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola already has another injury to deal with after the team failed to come through this summer's first pre-season friendly against Sunderland unscathed

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola will be without the injured Joe Gomez for around a month (Image: ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Joe Gomez sustained a muscle injury during Liverpool's first pre-season friendly against Sunderland. The Reds' head coach believes "it will be impossible" to have him available for the start of the Premier League season.

‌



Gomez, 29, lasted just eight minutes of the match in Nashville before having to be substituted. Ifeanyi Ndukwe replaced Liverpool's longest-serving player, who handed the captain's armband over to Kostas Tsimikas, who has returned from a loan at Roma this summer.

‌



The former England international was absent from their match overnight against Wrexham. Gomez now faces a month on the sidelines.

‌



Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool READ MORE :

Iraola offered an injury update on Thursday during a press conference in Chicago: "Joe has a muscle injury. It was quite clear since he complained straight away, so he will be off for some weeks.

"It's a muscle injury. It's difficult to say - normally one month. If it goes very well, then a little bit less. If it goes bad, then a bit more, but it's a muscle injury.

"It's not massive. I think it will be impossible to have him at the start of the season because we are not that far, but it shouldn't be much more."

‌



View 2 Images Joe Gomez is due to be missing for the next month with a muscle injury (Image: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

"Yesterday, Luke Chambers played there - he's not a centre-back, but he played really well. Until we recover some bodies - I think Jeremy [Jacquet] is ready to go."

Iraola continued: "A lot of players have surprised me, especially the young players I did not know before. The senior players, you have played against them and know them.

"The young players have given a very, very high level in these friendlies. They have to grow, which is very good. We will recover players; it would not be good if we played against Newcastle the same 11 we did yesterday.

Sports.title: Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest caught out as Premier League gambling ban bites
Sports.content:
Three Premier League teams are poised to start the 2026/27 season without front-of-shirt sponsors after falling to navigate the market in the wake of a ban on gambling companies.

It was way back in April 2023 when Premier League clubs agreed to get rid of gambling companies on the front of their shirts. And yet Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest have so far been unable to find a suitable replacement.

Obscure gambling companies had become part of the furniture of elite football, delighted to pay millions to for brand exposure - often in markets where gambling is illegal. Premier League sides were more than happy to accept their money - often worth double the offers from non-gambling companies - despite ethical concerns.

After mounting pressure, including from the government, that came to an end this summer. Eleven of the 20 teams in the Premier League last season had a gambling company emblazoned on their shirt. Three of those were relegated, leaving eight teams that needed to find a replacement this summer.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Six have been successful, but alongside Chelsea - who have had their own sponsor struggles in recent years - Sunderland and Forest look set to go sponsor-less 22 days before the season kicks off. Inside the commercial teams of Premier League clubs, gambling sponsors had been viewed as too good to turn down. They paid more than other companies and wanted less in return, acting as a simple billboard to millions of viewers.

While Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brentford, Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham managed to secure new sponsors, likely on reduced rates, Sunderland and Forest have held out. Sean Connell, editor of The Sponsor, an independent sponsorship research and valuation publication, believes they have become victim of " the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment" in Premier League history. In short, commercial teams have been forced to do more work for less reward.

"It’s an incredibly competitive sponsorship market," he tells Mirror Football. "The number of brands willing to put their hands in their pocket and stump up £5m to £15m to sponsor a Premier League club is already significantly reduced due to factors outside the sports landscape.

‌



View 4 Images Sunderland have gone from gambling company W88 to no sponsor (Image: Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images)

"Sponsors are under incredible amount of scrutiny to justify their expenditure. Then there's an unusually high number of teams in the market looking for a sponsor – in a normal year it might only be one or two, but it was 11 this summer.

"The gambling ban has taken what was already a shrinking pool of sponsors and removed a healthy chunk of those. It’s created what I believe is the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment that Premier League clubs have ever faced."

The gambling ban has been looming for over three years and Connell believes some have been guilty of failing to burying their heads in the sand. Mirror Football contacted Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest to request comment.

‌



Premier League front-of-shirt sponsors 2026/27 Arsenal – Emirates (Airline) Aston Villa – Visit Rwanda (Tourism) Bournemouth – Vitality (Insurance) Brentford – Indeed (Employment) Brighton – American Express (Bank) Chelsea – NONE Coventry – Monzo (Bank) Crystal Palace – Temporal (Software platform) Everton – CMC Markets (Financial services) Fulham – ClickHouse (Technology) Hull City – Corendon Airlines (Airline) Ipswich – Halo (Software) Leeds – Red Bull (Drinks) Liverpool – Standard Chartered (Bank) Manchester City – Etihad Airways (Airline) Manchester United – Snapdragon (Electronics) Newcastle – Knox (Sports drinks) Nottingham Forest – NONE (previously Bally’s) Sunderland – NONE (previously W88) Tottenham – AIA (Insurance)

“The profits and revenue have been so much greater than they would have been that nobody has taken any meaningful strides to address this," Connell says. "They have continued to take the money while the sun shone. Now some like Forest and Sunderland are in a difficult position.

“I think the clubs have been waiting to see what the highest possible deal is at the last possible moment. For some clubs that strategy worked out, for others like Sunderland and Forest they have presumably determined that the value of the deal on the table is not adequate and that holding out rather than underselling is the best strategy.”

Chelsea's situation is different. Remarkably, the Blues have not had a permanent front‑of‑shirt sponsor since their deal with Three ended in 2023. In February they announced a front-of-shirt deal until the end of the season with AI technology company IFS, but are now once again sponsor-less.

‌



View 4 Images Nottingham Forest have been unable to replace their gambling sponsor (Image: Gualter Fatia/Getty Images)

It has been reported that Chelsea have been holding out for £65m per season for their front-of-shirt sponsorship. Yet their 10th-place finish, and failure to secure any European football next season, appears to have damaged their chances.

While the gambling ban has undoubtedly impacted the revenues of Premier League clubs, particularly those outside the elite, who have more pulling power, it is a landmark moment in the league. R esearch in 2023 found that betting logos appear up to 3,500 times during TV games, a troubling reality for vulnerable people and gambling addicts.

Will Prochaska, director of the Coalition to End Gambling Ads (CEGA), said: “Andy Burnham has said we should 'relegate gambling sponsorship of sport to the history books' and we agree.

‌



View 4 Images Gambling sponsors had been ubiquitous in the Premier League (Image: Mark Fletcher/Getty Images)

“Fans will have little sympathy with clubs struggling to replace front-of-shirt gambling sponsors, and there's more than enough money in the game to ensure football can thrive without gambling revenues.

“Formula 1 cried foul that ending tobacco sponsorship would destroy the sport, but it's gone from strength to strength. Ridding football of its links to the gambling sector is an opportunity to turn a corner, not a burden.”

While gambling companies are still allowed on the sleeves of shirts in the Premier League, the gambling gold rush, when millions flowed into the game from obscure gambling entities operating via “white label” agreements with a company in the Isle of Man, are over. The results will be obvious come the first weekend of the season.

‌

Sports.title: 'No Plan B': Will Matthias Jaissle have tactical flexibility Eddie Howe never showed at Newcastle?
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United manager, bringing to a close a hugely successful five-year spell in which the former Bournemouth boss took the Magpies back into the Champions League and ended a 56-year wait for a trophy by beating Liverpool in the EFL Cup final.

However, Howe increasingly faced criticism for not developing a successful 'Plan B' to his brand of high-intensity, physical football, which saw results suffer when fatigue, the demand of European football, and injuries impacted his first-choice team.

AI 'supercomputer' Machine Football's analysis of the manager widely expected to take over from Howe, current Al Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle, shows how his style of play has evolved over time and could be just what Newcastle need to once again instil a clear identity.

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

How Jaissle's style has evolved

2023/24:

‌



Jaissle's first Al Ahli side were what Machine Football categorises as 'high-octane pressers', setting up for the majority of games in a 4-2-3-1 formation and relying heavily on dribbling and forward carries alongside an aggressive press.

That approach delivered 1.85 points per game and continental qualification. But Jaissle did not stop there, evolving his side further ahead of the following season.

2024/25:

Al Ahli developed into what Machine Football categorises as 'aggressive disruptors', with the emphasis shifting away from wing play and towards creating higher-quality chances with expected goals rising from 1.59 per 90 to 1.97 and points per game increasing to 2.04.

‌



Your Machine Football glossary of football tactics, data and stats buzzwords READ MORE :

2025/26:

Next, Jaissle added flexibility without changing the identity. Alongside the primary 4-2-3-1 setup - which he used in more than 40% of games - the German introduced a 4-3-3 variation in 22% of his games and, in roughly one match out of every five, more of a low-block counter style of play built on a traditional 4-4-2.

While the formations may have varied, the approach didn't. Al Ahli's PPDA (presses per defensive action - a pressing measurement where the lower the score, the more aggressive the press) was a high-octane 9.02.

Al Ahli also averaged 7.18 through passes per game – well above the Saudi Pro League average of 4.13 – and 19.83 touches inside the opposition box, comfortably ahead of the league average of 16.46.

‌



Rather than dominating possession, Al Ahli look to win the ball high and attack quickly. That approach resulted in Jaissle's best domestic season yet, averaging 2.38 points per game while winning a second consecutive AFC Champions League Elite title.

View 4 Images Cohesion: Newcastle v Al Ahli (2025/26). Al Ahli's weaker connections between defensive and midfield lines reflects their preference for vertical passes rather than slow build-up (Image: Machine Football)

Howe's 'flip-flopping' tactical approach

Who Jaissle is tactically suggests a significant change from the Newcastle side he looks set to inherit. The contrast becomes clearer when the numbers are put side by side.

The perception that Howe never managed to successfully implement a 'Plan B' comes from a run of seasons where the club's fortunes flip-flopped. Newcastle's style clearly changed from season to season during his tenure at St James' Park, but results also yo-yo'd.

‌



In 2022/23 Newcastle were what Machine Football's analysis classes as 'high-octane pressers' and enjoyed their best-ever points return (2.09 PPG).

The 2023/24 season, however, saw Champions League group stage football return and a shift towards a 'passive controllers' model accompany it.

In practice, Newcastle were playing more patient, lower-tempo football focused on control. It was still productive (1.72 PPG) but represented a step down in intensity and earned only a seventh placed Premier League finish.

In 2024/25 - no European football again - Howe swung back toward a more progressive, 'attacking engine' playing style. This helped their PPG bounce back up to 1.81 resulting in fifth place and Champions League qualification for a second time under Howe.

‌



Another flip then followed in 2025-26 as they moved into 'possession builders' - the most control-oriented identity of the four seasons - but only in just over half of their games, as PPG (1.26) reached its lowest ebb of any of Howe's four full seasons and Newcastle stuttered to 12th place in the league.

What this topsy-turvy playing identity suggests is that the new manager's style could help the Magpies get back to something like the best version of themselves from 22/23.

View 4 Images Stats comparison of Newcastle and Al Ahli 2025/26: Note how despite taking fewer shots, Al Ahli had a higher percentage of their efforts hit the target and a higher xG per 90 (Image: Machine Football)

Taking the stats from 2025-26, Newcastle and Al Ahli's possession is almost identical, but everything that follows is different. Last season, Al Ahli completed around 80 fewer passes per game - yet attempted more than twice as many through balls, created higher-quality chances and conceded almost half as many goals.

‌



Jaissle's style, then, is built entirely around progressing the ball quickly and attacking before opponents can reset.

Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier READ MORE :

Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit READ MORE :

Can Saudi success translate to Premier League?

While the change in approach might seem drastic, it looks set to get the Gallowgate End on its feet and - most importantly - the underlying numbers suggest it could translate into results, albeit with star players continuing to depart Newcastle.

Across 34 Saudi Pro League matches, Al Ahli scored 71 goals (2.09 per game), conceded just 25 (0.74 per game), kept 17 clean sheets and won 73.5% of their league matches.

Their expected goals total (66.73) closely mirrored their actual return, suggesting the attacking output is sustainable rather than the product of an unusually clinical season.

‌



View 4 Images A possible best XI for Jaissle's Newcastle based on the current options available (Image: Machine Football)

Newcastle's numbers tell a different story. They scored 53 goals in 38 Premier League games (1.39 per game), won just 36.8% of their matches and finished with expected goals for and against that were almost identical (59.23 xG versus 59.5 xGA).

The difference isn't how much of the ball the two teams have. It's what they do with it. Now all that's left is for Jaissle to prove he can make the same principles work in the Premier League.

‌

Sports.title: UEFA statement leaves FIFA with 37-day deadline as World Cup hangs in the balance
Sports.content:
UEFA statement leaves FIFA with 37-day deadline as World Cup hangs in the balance

With the football world turning in on itself after Gianni Infantino's controversial grand plan was wholeheartedly rejected by UEFA, a tournament is now at risk of collapsing

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's grand World Cup plans already have significant opposition (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto)

UEFA's pledge to boycott FIFA tournaments has seemingly put the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup at risk. The governing body of European football released an imposing statement in response to Gianni Infantino's plan.

‌



The president of FIFA recently unearthed plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors, promising to earn more money for each member nation who expresses support for his idea by September 19. This has been pushed back in the strongest possible way by UEFA and the FA, who insisted all of the 55 member nations will boycott all FIFA competitions for as long as this idea is still alive.

‌



It was a firm statement which came after a meeting held by UEFA president Alexander Ceferin. Assuming UEFA is true to its word, it appears the U20 Women's World Cup is at risk of becoming the first FIFA competition to be effected by this civil war.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

On September 5, the competition is set to begin with the final taking place 22 days later. The competition is being held in Poland and will feature 24 teams from all six FIFA confederations. Out of all of the nations in the group, six are from UEFA as Poland, Italy, England, Portugal, France and Spain are all expected to compete in the tournament. The other nations involved are Argentina, Mexico, Benin, Japan, New Zealand, the USA, Brazil, Tanzania, Canada, North Korea, Costa Rica, Colombia, South Korea, Ecuador, Ghana, Nigeria, New Caledonia and China.

At present, it's currently unclear as to what will happen with the competition. UEFA have made it clear they have no intention in representing any of their member nations in FIFA tournaments for as long as this idea is still going. Considering Infantino's hard deadline to express support is September 19, it's possible the boycott could last until then and beyond. The Swiss football figurehead has also claimed his idea only needs support from just over 50 per cent of its members for the idea to run.

‌



With 55 nations expressing their firm opposition to the idea, Infantino has already lost a firm chunk of potential support. However, other Confederations which include CONCACAF (North American nations), CONMEBOL (South American), the CAF (African Confederation) and Oceania are yet to make their feelings known.

What is clear from UEFA's intervention is that they want the idea to be quashed, quickly. In their statement, they wrote: "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

View 3 Images The future of the U-20 Women's World Cup is looking uncertain (Image: 2026 FIFA)

‌



"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

‌



"But our opposition goes far beyond process. The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

View 3 Images North Korea go into the competition as the defending champions (Image: AFP or licensors)

"This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

‌



"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

Sports.title: Liverpool signed highly-rated teen, 223-goal striker and title winner from PSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool signed highly-rated teen, 223-goal striker and title winner from PSG

Liverpool are continuing their pursuit of one Paris Saint-Germain star this summer

View 4 Images Liverpool have done a few deals with Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have a long history of getting deals done in the transfer market. And this working relationship could be strengthened if the Reds convince Bradley Barcola to head to Anfield.

‌



The club are set to open talks with PSG over a potential transfer for the winger. Initial talks with Barcola's representatives have prompted Liverpool to formalise their interest with an official approach.

‌



Andoni Iraola has been on the lookout for a wide player since Mohamed Salah's exit. Barcola has been on Liverpool's radar for some time, and the club will hope to make him their third summer signing.

‌



Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet have signed deals at Anfield, but there's certain to be more movement – both incoming and outgoing – before the new season starts. If Barcola does decide to join Liverpool, it wouldn't represent the first time that a transfer between the two clubs has taken place.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football examines some of the previous transfers between the two sides.

‌



Highly-rated teen

David Ngog signed his first professional contract with PSG in 2006 as a highly-rated teenager. Two years later, he arrived at Anfield as a fresh-faced 19-year-old under Rafael Benitez.

The striker would play under three different managers at Liverpool, including Roy Hodgson and Sir Kenny Dalglish. Ngog scored 19 goals and assisted six times across 94 appearances before leaving for Bolton Wanderers in 2011.

View 4 Images David Ngog spent three seasons with the Reds (Image: John Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Despite such a promising start to his career, Ngog really failed to reach the heights his early days promised. He later played for Swansea City, Reims, Panionios, Ross County and Budapest Honved before retiring in Lithuania at the age of 31.

223-goal striker

Nicolas Anelka had already played in the Premier League before joining Liverpool on loan in 2001. The striker left PSG for Arsenal at 17 and made 42 goal contributions from 1997 to 1999.

A move to Real Madrid came next before Anelka returned to France a year later. PSG then loaned the striker to Liverpool in the 2001 January transfer window.

‌



View 4 Images Nicolas Anelka has plenty of experience in the Premier League (Image: Clive Brunskill/ Getty Images)

The France international made 22 appearances for the Reds and scored five goals, helping the team to a second-placed finish in the Premier League. Gerard Houllier opted against giving Anelka a permanent deal at Liverpool and he ended up at Manchester City.

He came back to haunt the Reds after scoring a brace in a 2-1 win over them in May 2003. Throughout his career, Anelka scored 223 goals for club and country, winning two Champions League titles and the European Championship with France.

‌



PSG title winner

View 4 Images Mamadou Sakho was a title winner before he arrived at Anfield (Image: VI Images via Getty Images)

Mamadou Sakho had already made 201 appearances for PSG before his £18million move to Liverpool in 2013. The defender had won the Ligue 1 title just weeks before he joined the Reds, bringing a wealth of experience to Brendan Rodgers' side.

Sakho would go on to make 80 appearances for Liverpool, scoring three goals and continuing his time at Anfield after Rodgers was sacked in 2016. Jurgen Klopp kept the centre-half around for a half a season before Crystal Palace signed him on loan.

Article continues below

After an impressive temporary spell, Sakho would sign a permanent move to Palace in 2017 for a fee of £26m. He would go on to have stints at Montpellier and Torpedo Kutaisi before retiring in January this year at 35.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott has spoken out about his future under Andoni Iraola after spending a season on the sidelines at Aston Villa under Unai Emery

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott has already featured in two friendlies for Andoni Iraola this summer (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Harvey Elliott believes he has been gifted a second chance at Liverpool after the arrival of Andoni Iraola, following a disastrous loan to Aston Villa last season. The former Fulham youngster is back with the Reds for pre-season and has already featured for his new boss as he looks to take the opportunity to impress.

‌



The midfielder made just one Premier League start during his time at Villa Park and nine appearances in all due to a clause in his loan which would have triggered a £35m transfer after his tenth appearance. Elliott was left out of squads throughout the season as he struggled to play under Unai Emery.

‌



It was not the season Elliott wanted, having only started twice in the Premier League during Arne Slot's title-winning season at Anfield. It cost him any chance of making it into Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad and leaves him desperate to play football.

‌



Elliott holds no ill will toward Villa but is now firmly focused on establishing himself at Liverpool. He believes that with a new coaching staff to impress, he has the perfect opportunity to rekindle his career.

“Unfortunately, it didn't work out, but the way I see it is that's last season now, I'm here. It's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it," Elliott explained.

Liverpool's significant Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG close in on replacement READ MORE :

Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York READ MORE :

“Especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in. It's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their (good) books.

‌



"But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best, had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very, very well. Unfortunately, the situation happened, but It's another learning curve.

“It's a situation that I can take on in my career, and just keep looking forward. I'm here now, and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad."

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott barely featured for Aston Villa last season but did win the Europa League (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

While Elliott is looking to move on from last season, he conceded it was a difficult situation to bear. The 23-year-old was pleased to be part of an historic Europa League win with Villa but endured a draining situation on the sidelines.

“Mentally, it was a very tough one," he added. "As I said, it was a learning curve. It was an opportunity for me to experience something new, as much as I didn't want to do it, and I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all, but I have no hard feelings.

‌



“I wish them all the very best. Well, I did greatly have a lot of love for them. They treated me as one of their own, as it were, and for that. I respect them highly.

“But it was tough, mentally and physically, but I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it, and achieve something at the end of the season as well (with Villa winning the Europa League).

“That was another historical moment for the club, and to be part of that was another great situation. But my focus is on this season, at Liverpool, and I just need to see what happens.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
