World.title: Major police operation in Tallinn targets illegal migrants
World.content:
A large police operation took place Thursday in Tallinn's Nõmme district to apprehend suspected migrants. According to local residents, police also used drones during the operation.

Police received a call at 12:04 on Thursday reporting that several foreign nationals might be inside an apartment building in Tallinn's Nõmme district, with grounds to suspect they had entered the country illegally, said Indrek Aru, head of the border guard bureau at the Northern Prefecture.

Patrol officers responded and went to verify the information. At the scene, police detained 12 people suspected of illegally entering Estonia. They were taken to a detention center for initial procedural steps.

The tip about the suspicious foreign nationals came from a local resident.

Police continue checking the surrounding area to determine whether more people may have been in the apartment. "If you notice groups of foreign nationals who appear lost, differ from typical tourists, or are engaged in suspicious activity, it is worth informing the police," Aru said.

"Migration pressure on Estonia has increased in recent days. Over the past week, such detentions have occurred daily. We expect the pressure to continue in the coming months," he added.

On Wednesday, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) said it has apprehended 63 migrants this week, with no sign that the influx is slowing. Most migrants are entering Estonia from the Latvia–Belarus border, and authorities do not expect the flow to stop before poorer autumn weather arrives.

Interior Minister Igor Taro said Belarus is behind the migration pressure, sending migrants to the Baltic states at Russia's encouragement.

PPA director Egert Belitšev added Wednesday that the focal point of hybrid warfare has shifted toward the Baltic states and Finland, as Poland–Lithuania and Poland–Germany border crossings have begun implementing additional controls.

According to Belitšev, the migration situation has worsened specifically this week, with 63 migrants detained — bringing the yearly total to 102, compared with 39 at the same time last year.

The arrival of such numbers of illegal migrants places additional strain not only on the PPA but also on the court system and local municipalities.

World.title: Tram to Tallinn Airport reopens in August
World.content:
Tallinn's airport tramline was officially reopened on Thursday by representatives from the City of Tallinn, the Ministry of Climate and Rail Baltic, ahead of its relaunch on August 1.

From the start of next month, the airport will be served by two tram lines: T2 (Kopli – Old Town – Airport) and T4 (Tondi – Airport).

To maintain a connection to Suur-Paala, the city is launching a new tram line, T6 (Kopli – Hobujaama – Suur-Paala). Due to construction work on Peterburi Road, the line will begin service in late August. During the construction period, buses will temporarily serve the Suur-Paala area.

Due to changes in the tram network, Tallinn Transport has also updated its timetables.

Going forward, tram lines T1 (Kopli – Kadriorg), T2 (Kopli – Lennujaam), T3 (Tondi – Kadriorg), T4 (Tondi – Lennujaam), and T6 (Kopli – Suur-Paala) will depart every 10 minutes. Line T5 (Kopli – Vana-Lõuna) will depart every 20 minutes.

The airport tram connection was suspended in 2023 due to the construction of the Vanasadam tram line and later the construction of the Ülemiste train terminal.

World.title: Report says Estonia's working life could stretch to 45 years as lifespans rise
World.content:
Eurostat projects that Estonians could live to 85 within the next 50 years, pushing average working life toward 45 years — a shift that would force people to relearn skills or even change careers multiple times, according to a new report from the Foresight Center.

Eneli Kindsiko, an expert at the Foresight Center, says that as life expectancy increases, working life inevitably becomes longer, and education obtained in youth is no longer sufficient for an entire career.

"You cannot expect education received in youth to provide knowledge for the next 40–50 years of work. Yet many people stop learning already in middle age. Today, all of Europe faces the question of how to ensure lifelong learning in an aging society," Kindsiko said.

Currently, Estonia's expected working life is 41.5 years. The report's authors argue that in the future, Estonia will need a continuous learning system that allows people to regularly upgrade skills, retrain and change professional direction throughout a nearly 45‑year career.

Eneli Kindsiko. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

According to the forecast by Statistics Estonia, by 2050, people aged over 65 will make up 27% of the Estonian population, compared to 20% currently.

The World Economic Forum estimates that by 2030, 39% of today's key skills will become outdated, and 59 out of every 100 employees will need additional training.

Although Estonia exceeds the EU average in adult participation in learning, most learners are 25–49 years old, predominantly women with higher education.

Adults with low education levels, people with reduced work ability and older men participate in training the least.

The report notes that later‑career learning opportunities depend heavily on employer support, access to training programs and personal motivation.

The OECD considers mid‑career the most challenging period: balancing work and family responsibilities makes learning difficult, even though the labor market demands constant skill renewal. As retirement approaches, the risk of losing connection with the labor market and social life increases.

These findings align with PIAAC (Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies) adult‑skills data, which show the highest skill levels among people aged 26–35, followed by a gradual decline. After age 55, participation in additional training drops sharply: only about 10% of people aged 55–64 engage in upskilling.

The report "Lengthening Working Life and Lifelong Learning" was prepared as part of a study on the development of Estonia's lifelong learning system through 2050. The Foresight Center at the Riigikogu analyzes long‑term social and economic trends and prepares development forecasts for the country.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Turkey seeks comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement with Iraq following discussions with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara.

Erdogan said that Turkey’s state-owned oil and gas company, TPAO, will operate at Iraq’s Kirkuk oilfield, which is now being developed by British Petroleum (BP), during a joint press conference following a signing ceremony that had been expected to extend the Kirkuk-Ceyhan oil pipeline deal for another year, according to Reuters.

The agreement to renew the decades-old pipeline contract, which regulates shipments along the strategic route, expired on Monday.

After signing three agreements, Erdogan noted that additional deals were anticipated. However, his ministers promptly briefed him on stage, and the two leaders continued with their statements without announcing any further agreements.

The agreement between Iraq and Turkey regarding the crude oil pipeline expired on July 27.

“Our goal is to complete an energy cooperation deal that benefits both parties as quickly as possible,” Erdogan said.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said in a statement on X that TPAO has bought a 15 percent stake in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BPECKL), enabling the Turkish business to operate in the sector.

Bayraktar explained the TPAO will cooperate with BPECKL to raise oil production at the Kirkuk field, which has reserves estimated at three million barrels.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to India fall as New Delhi diversifies import sources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping via the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Indian refiners confirmed they have secured their crude oil requirements until the end of September and have begun arranging purchases for the fourth quarter of the year, despite persistent concerns about the impact of any interruptions to shipping routes on global supply chains.

Meanwhile, Russia remained India’s top crude oil supplier in the first half of the year, while imports from the UAE and Brazil increased.

India’s purchases from Iraq and the United States fell as New Delhi attempted to diversify its supply sources and reduce the risks associated with reliance on a single source.

Indian refiners have warned that increased shipping risks and higher insurance costs, along with declining discounts on Russian oil, are affecting profit margins.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Six Iranian advisors killed in US-Saudi attack on Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A joint US-Saudi attack on targets in Iraq killed six Iranian advisors on Wednesday, according to two Iraqi officials who spoke to the Associated Press (AP).

A meeting that was set for Thursday in Saudi Arabia between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was called off due to recent attacks by armed groups targeting Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi ordered an emergency meeting of Iraq’s National Security Council following the coordinated attacks on the country.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell said in a statement that the meeting was ordered in response to the evolving security situation and the airstrikes that targeted several Iraqi provinces early on Wednesday.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Wednesday that US forces, in cooperation with Saudi armed forces, carried out precision airstrikes targeting sites linked to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The coordinated airstrikes were in retaliation for a series of drone attacks targeting US interests and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM said in a statement that the strikes, carried out on July 28, targeted logistics sites and weapons depots allegedly used by Iranian-backed groups. It added that these groups were directed by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to attack US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

US and Saudi fighter jets carried out the strikes, an operation described by CENTCOM as a strong response to more than 30 drone attacks that the IRGC had conducted in the past few days.

Headquarters and sites belonging to the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in several Iraqi provinces were targeted by the US-Saudi airstrikes in the country.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes test Iraq’s fragile security balance
World.content:
Baghdad – US-Saudi strikes on Iraq killed at least 20 militants, including several Iranians, on Wednesday, according to the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance that includes pro-Iran groups.

The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

The Hashed al-Shaabi, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), said that at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll”.

Two Hashed officials told AFP that five Iranian advisors were among those killed in a strike in the central province of Diyala.

AFP correspondents saw coffins wrapped in Iranian flags during a funeral organised by the Hashed al-Shaabi in Baghdad for those killed.

The Hashed alliance was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before it was formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces.

It now includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.

US President Donald Trump said the strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, according to Fox News.

They follow growing US pressure on Baghdad to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have frequently targeted US facilities in the country and have long called for the withdrawal of US troops.

Iraq’s new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Earlier this month, Zaidi visited both the United States and Iran.

– ‘Inevitable response’ –

The strikes came after Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming the Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

The most active pro-Iran armed groups are united under an alliance known as the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, which has acted in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks against US bases in Iraq and across the region.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq said “our response to the American enemy is inevitable, and may target its tools in Saudi Arabia”.

But the group added that it would only retaliate after the Arbaeen day of pilgrimage, which falls on Tuesday.

The Arbaeen marks one of the most significant events in the Shia Muslim calendar, during which pilgrims, many from Iran, flock to Iraq to visit the holy shrines.

The pro-Iran groups denied attacking Saudi Arabia and they haven’t claimed any attacks since the US-Iran war resumed earlier this month.

– Violation –

Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects “all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented.”

The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would “confront any violation of Iraq’s sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states”.

It reaffirmed its commitment to ensure the state’s monopoly over weapons.

Zaidi’s government has given those groups that Washington designates as terrorist organisations until September 30 to disarm.

Oil-rich Iraq has been trying to move past decades of war and unrest, but it remains vulnerable to regional and internal flare-ups.

World.title: Iraq condemns US-Saudi strikes, vows tighter control over armed groups
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq condemned U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday that targeted Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites, calling the attacks a violation of its sovereignty, and announced new measures to tighten state control over security and prevent Iraqi territory from being used to threaten neighboring countries.

Following the attacks, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, which the government said killed and injured many Iraqis.

As regional tensions rose, Al-Zaidi cancelled a planned visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

In a statement published after the meeting, the council said that the strikes happened when Baghdad was already in talks with US and Saudi authorities over suspicions that Iran-aligned armed organizations operating from Iraq committed drone assaults on Saudi land.

“The government was actively engaging with the relevant parties to verify and address the concerns raised by both the Saudi and US sides,” the statement stated, adding that the military action hampered such efforts.

The council authorized a comprehensive security strategy aimed at strengthening state authority across Iraq, combating breaches of Iraqi sovereignty, and prohibiting any party from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The steps reflect Baghdad’s efforts to guarantee that no armed organization may launch assaults from Iraqi soil that could pull the nation into larger regional wars, while also confirming the government’s goal of bringing all security actions under state control.

The council also directed the Foreign Ministry to take legal and diplomatic measures under international law and the United Nations Charter to record the attacks and protect Iraq’s legal rights.

The government condemned the attacks but emphasized that responding to security threats and enforcing the law is solely the responsibility of Iraq’s constitutional institutions.

“The government rejects all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented,” the statement read.

The council underlined Baghdad’s commitment to addressing regional conflicts via diplomacy while maintaining efforts to keep all armaments under state control.

It also restated Iraq’s commitment to carrying out the security agreement guiding the departure of the US-led international coalition by the end of September 2026.

The emergency conference occurred hours after US President Donald Trump claimed that the midnight attacks were coordinated with the Iraqi government, something Baghdad has not officially verified.

Iraqi authorities have openly opposed the operation, emphasizing the political sensitivity of the attacks.

The events highlight Al-Zaidi’s increasingly precarious situation, as he seeks to boost Iraq’s connections with the US and Gulf Arab governments while retaining relations with Iran.

His decision to cancel the Saudi visit underlines the gravity of the problem, as Baghdad seeks to temper regional tensions while preventing Iraqi land from becoming a battlefield for opposing forces.

The government’s current security strategy also suggests a renewed desire to prevent armed groups from operating outside official control, as Baghdad wants to reassure neighboring nations that Iraq will not be used as a springboard for assaults that endanger regional peace.

World.title: Uptime Institute partners with T964 to expand Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Uptime Institute, based in the United States, and Iraqi digital infrastructure company Tech964 Holding Limited (T964) have formed a strategic partnership to help develop Iraq’s digital infrastructure, marking the latest technology agreement to result from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s investment-focused visit to Washington.

The agreement, signed earlier this month at the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit hosted by the US Chamber of Commerce, names T964 as Uptime Institute’s business partner in Iraq to promote international data center standards, professional training, and the development of resilient digital infrastructure.

The agreement is part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy beyond oil by increasing digital infrastructure, attracting technological investment, and bolstering industries including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, and cybersecurity.

T964, one of Iraq’s major private digital infrastructure businesses, has announced that it would collaborate with the Uptime Institute to implement internationally recognized standards for the country’s expanding network of data centers, as well as increase technical competence and operational best practices.

The partnership is anticipated to help establish carrier-neutral data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud services, and AI-ready digital platforms, all of which the government believes are important to modernizing public services and stimulating private-sector investment.

The pact follows a series of technological ties announced during Al-Zaidi’s tour to the United States, during which Iraq inked more than 50 agreements totaling more than $60 billion in the energy, banking, infrastructure, industrial, and technology sectors.

Improving digital infrastructure has become a key component of Iraq’s long-term economic plan, as the country strives to lessen reliance on oil earnings and establish a knowledge-based economy capable of attracting foreign technology businesses while also encouraging homegrown innovation.

The alliance also underscores increased US private-sector interest in Iraq’s digital economy, especially as demand for secure data centers, cloud computing capacity, and AI infrastructure in the Middle East grows.

Iraq has increasingly prioritized digital infrastructure for foreign investment alongside energy and transportation, with officials claiming that internationally certified data centers and modern telecommunications networks will be critical to supporting e-government services, digital banking, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthening Iraq’s role as an emerging regional technology hub.

World.title: 'Your skin brighter than country's future': Abhijeet Dipke's jab at PM Modi's late night video

PM Modi and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke (R)

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on late Thursday mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his latest late-night video message to students where he highlighted recently passed anti-paper leak Bill.Dipke, whose platform grew into a massive student protest and culminated in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister, took to Instagram to target the Prime Minister.Commenting on PM Modi's video, Dipke wrote, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."Prime Minister Narendra Modi Thursday night released a fresh video message after Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, calling it as a major step towards building a more reliable examination system and cracking down on paper leak mafias.In a video posted on social media, PM Modi said, "Friends, we have been taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Whether it is setting up special task forces, establishing fast-track courts, or incorporating suggestions from the states, we have been working continuously in this direction."He said paper leaks had plagued governments across the country for decades. "Every state government and every central government has faced the problem of paper leaks over the past several decades. Because of this, the future of our children has also been put at risk," he said.The Prime Minister added that the government had recognised the need for reforms in the education system and greater use of technology to safeguard the integrity of examinations.

World.title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The debate on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill in RS Thursday turned into a heated argument between treasury benches and opposition when leader of the opposition

read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti.

Kharge alleged portions of Manusmriti have become part of the "curriculum" under BJP govt. He was challenged by leader of the House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.

RS chairperson CP Radhakrishnan asked Kharge what Manusmriti had to do with the bill. Kharge claimed, "Manusmriti teaches that if a 'Shudra' listens to Veda, his ears should be filled with shards; if he reads Ved aloud, his tongue should be cut off; and if he retains its words, his body should be dismembered."

BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Kharge citing B R Ambedkar's writings to argue there was no untouchability in the era of Manu.

World.title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP
World.content:
BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi speaks in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests, as they highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns by holding dialogue with students to end their agitation and proposing a stronger law against exam paper leaks.Participating in the discussion, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest and also highlighted how senior ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh held talks with them and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was fasting for 26 days.Government agreed to the demands of students, he said, adding Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, a fast-track court was set up and a task force was set up by PM Narendra Modi under Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.On Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Trivedi said there are three basic principles - a sensitive approach towards students, a secured process and a stringent law against paper leaks. Trivedi said the bill provides for stringent punishment, time-bound investigation and speedier justice. These will prove key in preventing paper leaks, he said.Targeting opposition MPs, who raised questions on PM Modi's educational qualifications, he said those who have never themselves faced competition in exams, in education, or in their own political parties are now teaching the govt. "In contrast, our politicians and our PM have faced competition and exams and have risen from the ground," Trivedi said.JDU's Sanjay Jha supported the bill, saying this should not be looked at from political prospects.Shiv Sena's Milind Deora suggested students should be involved in the reform process by giving them a formal role in the consultations.

World.title: ‘Normal’ July rain defies forecast of El Nino impact
World.content:
Monsoon in India (representative image)

El NiÃ±o alone can no more explain Indiaâs rain pattern: Experts

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Indiaâs monsoon has delivered a surprise this July, defying forecasts of below-normal rainfall despite a strengthening El Nino and reinforcing scientistsâ warnings that climate change is altering the countryâs most important weather system, report Chittaranjan Tembhekar & Gaurav Talwar.As of July 30, India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. IMD had said July rainfall was likely to be less than 94% of long period average.However, rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.The monsoon deficit since June 1 was 14%. The unexpected turnaround in July has eased fears of a big monsoon shortfall but highlighted a new reality: long dry spells interspersed with short bursts of extremely heavy rain capable of triggering floods and landslides.According to a Climate Trends briefing, successive weather systems cut the national rainfall deficit considerably from 40% at the end of June.Scientists say the biggest lesson from monsoon 2026 is that El NiÃ±o alone can no longer explain Indiaâs rainfall behaviour.Global warming, warming oceans and changing atmospheric circulation are increasingly interacting with traditional climate drivers, making monsoon forecasts more difficult.âThe challenge is no longer predicting how much rain India will receive, but forecasting where, when and how intensely it will fall in a warming climate,â scientists said.Rainfall remained highly uneven. While 16 meteorological subdivisions states recorded normal rainfall in the season and three saw excess to large-excess rainfall, 17 subdivisions remained deficient. Central India was almost normal with a 1% surplus, northwest India had an 11% shortfall, while east and northeast India remained 30% below normal and south India 25% deficient.The findings are particularly striking because the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has projected an 81% probability of a very strong El NiÃ±o developing between Oct and Dec â a pattern usually associated with weaker Indian monsoons.Former IMD director general K J Ramesh attributed Julyâs recovery to abnormal warming over the western Pacific, which spawned successive monsoon systems over the Bay of Bengal, and the increasing influence of Western Disturbances that enhanced rainfall over Maharashtra and Gujarat.âClimate change is reshaping the characteristics of the monsoon, which existing models are failing to take into account,â Ramesh said.Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading said the monsoon rebounded rapidly after an early July lull. He cited Umbergaon in Gujarat receiving 1,064 mm of rain in 24 hours âamong the highest daily totals recorded since 1901 â as evidence of intensifying rainfall extremes, adding that climate change appears to be amplifying the monsoonâs internal weather systems.

World.title: Why’s CJI not on panel to pick CEC, Supreme Court asks government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners,

on Thursday said

must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include

in the selection panel.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma said the CJI was part of selection panels for CBI director and Lokpal, and asked what could be the reason for excluding him from the process of selecting CEC and ECs â posts that are among the most important for a democracy. The court reserved its verdict on the Centreâs plea that the matter be referred to a constitution bench.

The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act, under which CEC and ECs are appointed by President on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of PM, leader of the opposition, and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by PM.

SG Tushar Mehta argued that the court could not begin with an assumption that the PM would act against democratic principles.

People must trust PMâs decisions, says SG Mehta amid challenge to authority

In 2023, a five-judge constitution bench of SC had directed that pending enactment of a law by Parliament, appointments should be made by a panel comprising the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition to infuse independence into the process. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a cabinet minister.





Attorney general (AG) R Venkataramani and solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta urged the bench not to question the wisdom of Parliament, arguing that doing so would amount to interference with the independence of the legislature. The AG said Parliamentâs legislative choice could not be questioned merely because another model was possible, and that âParliament cannot be gaggedâ. The SG added that the three organs of the state â executive, legislature and judiciary â were independent, and their independence must be respected.

âPeople must trust the Prime Minister. The office of the Prime Minister has a sanctity attachedâ¦ If his decision is not to be trusted and is to be seen as necessarily a bad-faith exercise, then why not have a provision that even while selecting his cabinet he must consult some former judge or outsider?â SG Mehta said.

Mehta added that one organ of the state could not proceed on the basis that the PM and other ministers would act in bad faith or against constitutional principles simply because they have the numerical majority.

The bench clarified that there was no question of not trusting the PM. However, it asked the SG how many ministers in the government had cases pending against them, recalling that the court had earlier reposed trust in the elected government to ensure that people with criminal antecedents were not appointed as ministers.

âIt is not a lack of faith. The election commissioner has to be an independent person. Should there not be a show of fairness? We are not saying fairness has not been achieved by this committee.

Just like justice is not only to be done, it has to be shown to be done, we are on the second part,â the bench said.

Government requested that the petitions be referred to a larger constitution bench, arguing that an important question of law was involved. This plea was strongly opposed by senior advocates D Seshadri Naidu, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Prashant Bhushan and Sanjay Parikh, who contended that government was raising this ground after 20 days of hearing and should not be allowed to do so.

In an affidavit, government countered the petitionersâ claim that the independence of Election Commission would be compromised by replacing CJI with a cabinet minister. It maintained that there was no flaw in the law passed by Parliament, and that free and fair elections had never been casualties even when appointments were made solely by the executive for over seven decades.

Government described as hypothetical the suggestion that vesting the executive with exclusive authority in EC appointments would necessarily compromise the independence of the poll watchdog.

World.title: Anti-paper leak bill clears Parliament; PM Modi says it will build a credible exam system
World.content:
Amid oppositionâs walkout, Rajya Sabha clears it by voice vote

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Parliament on Thursday approved a bill to amend the anti-paper leak law, prescribing stricter punishment, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi saying an important step towards building a credible exam system has been taken.In a selfie-video message, the Prime Minister asserted that gangs behind exam paper leaks, which play with the future of students, will not be spared, and stringent laws are needed to deal with them. "Our work will continue and we will not allow this situation to persist for long," he said.For the past many decades every state govt and the Centre have faced this menace of paper leaks, which is posing a crisis for students, the PM said about the bill that proposes a longer jail term and steeper fine. "It has become necessary to bring reforms in the education system in all states and at the Centre," Modi said, asking the youth to work together with govt to fulfil the dream of a developed India.His government, he said, has taken a series of steps for reforming the exam system, be it forming a task force, constituting fast-track courts or taking into consideration the views of states. Optimal use of technology is necessary, he added.Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, was cleared by voice vote in RS amid a walkout by a large section of the opposition, a day after it was passed by LS. This will become a law after the President's assent.Replying to the discussion on the bill in Rajya Sabha, Union minister Jitendra Singh highlighted measures taken by govt in the education sector, including NEP-2020 and an increase in the number of universities.Earlier in the day, Singh had told the Upper House that the bill testifies the govt does not stand on prestige and is open to healthy inputs. "We are open to constructive suggestions from all quarters, and that's exactly the reason why, in the wake of the recent sequence of events, the PM lost no time to declare that nobody will be allowed to jeopardise the future of our children and also announced the resolve of zero tolerance to paper leaks," he said.According to the bill, individuals involved in paper leaks or unfair means in exams will get jail terms for a minimum of five years and a maximum of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh. For organised crimes, it proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. The bill also seeks to empower all state govts and UT administrations to designate any court of session as a special fast-track court to try offences under the proposed law.The bill also empowers the central govt to constitute a special task force for the investigation of any offence, if necessary.

World.title: 16 Indians, including 10 seamen, killed in Middle East conflict: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict earlier this year, sixteen Indian nationals, including 10 seafarers, have lost their lives in the region (eight in Oman, four in UAE, two in Kuwait and one each in Iran and Saudi Arabia) and 75 have been injured, said the government in Parliament.

Responding to a written question in Rajya Sabha, MoS (MEA) Kirti Vardhan Singh said that in a separate accident not related to attacks, 12 Indian nationals lost their lives in Ras Laffan Gas Facility in Qatar.

"Government, in coordination with the host governments, has extended all possible assistance to the families of the deceased Indian nationals for early repatriation of the mortal remains to India.

The injured Indian nationals received medical treatment in local hospitals.

Indian Embassies and Consulates coordinated with the local authorities and the hospitals for regular updates on the health condition and extended all required assistance," said the minister.

World.title: Women push back against eviction in south Kolkata slum
World.content:
Women domestic workers of a south Kolkata slum in Dhakuria are pushing back against an eviction notice which does not ensure their rehabilitation. They have started a 24-hour sit-in demonstration under the Dhakuria flyover where they stay, since Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

At least 58 families live under the Dhakuria bridge, on one side of the road. Of these, 43 families have documents to prove their residence in the area. The slum dwellers on the other side of the bridge are yet to get an eviction notice, but many are counting days.

“They are coming in with police, central forces, police cars, and issuing notices, intimidating us late at night. Every time a police car comes by, everyone‘s face fills with fear, that they are minutes away from losing their home,” Sapna Tripathi, a member of the West Bengal Domestic Workers Union said.

Ms. Tripathi is not a resident of the area but comes every day to help the locals of the area organise and agitate, as well as assisting them with legal paperwork. She asked where these families would go overnight in the heavy monsoon rains of Bengal. They have also visited the “Janatar Darbar” (face-to-face interaction with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to showcase people’s problems) but they failed to meet him. They also claim that they were turned away and told that the eviction is an administrative decision and the political party cannot do anything about it.

“Does anyone in this world like to live in slums and under bridges? Do we stay here voluntarily? We are forced to stay here because we are poor,” Ratna Parua, a local woman said. She said that every government office has told them that they have “orders from higher ups and their hands are tied.”

Locals have visited the local MLA Swapan Dasgupta’s office but failed to meet him. The local police or civic bodies have also not been of much help, according to the women. They have filed a case at the Calcutta High Court but were able to get a stay order on the eviction notice for just one day. They are waiting for the case to be heard in court again.

A young college going woman said that the anxiety of losing the roof over her head has affected her studies. “I submitted a project to college, and it was all wrong. I am not able to take this pressure; I am not able to concentrate on my studies. Just because we are poor, do we not deserve basic humanitarian consideration?” the girl said wishing to remain anonymous.

Many like her are spending sleepless nights and agitating and raising slogans to stop the feared bulldozer action. But they have refused to budge without their grievances being heard and proper rehabilitation.

Almost 90% of these women work as domestic helps in the nearby posh localities and high-rise buildings and the men work as daily wagers. They take turns sitting at the protest site, as every missed day of work means lost wages.

“Will the wheel of society turn without our labour? Will these houses which employ us function without us cooking, cleaning, driving their cars, working as their security? But when development and beautification of a place happens, why does it exclude us, the ones who keep society moving?” Bibha Naskar, secretary of the West Bengal Domestic Workers Union, who is also a resident of the area told The Hindu on Wednesday (July 29).

Ms. Naskar said that all of the residents of this locality voted for the new government and helped them come to power, but they are now feeling betrayed by the same administration they supported in the Assembly elections.

Since the Bharatiya Janta Party came to power in West Bengal on May 4, bulldozer demolitions and eviction of hawkers and slum dwellers across the State have been widespread. Human rights activists and opposition parties have also criticised the crackdown on the poorer sections of society.

World.title: Trump mulling $1,00,000 fee for students keen to work in U.S. after graduation: report
World.content:
The U.S. is planning to impose a $1,00,000 fee on visas issued to international students for working in the U.S. after graduation from an American university, The Wall Street Journal reported.

The Trump administration move comes after a U.S. court struck down a proposal to levy a $1,00,000 fee on H1-B visas.

According to The Wall Street Journal, the Department of Homeland Security is mulling the high fee on Optional Practical Training (OPT) visas which are an extension of F-1 visas issued to students.

The OPT programme allows foreign graduates to work for one to three years on their student visas in areas directly related to their studies.

Roughly 4,19,000 foreigners were working on OPT in 2024, the latest year for which data are available.

Tech companies, which conduct most of the recruitments from U.S. universities, opposed the $1,00,000 fee on H1-B visas.

A DHS spokeswoman said in a statement: “No policies should be considered final until formally announced. At DHS we are always having conversations about how to use all tools in our arsenal to protect the integrity of our legal immigration system.” In addition to the H-1B and student visas, officials at the State Department are also weighing attaching a $1,00,000 bond on applicants for green cards outside the U.S., redeemable only after they move to the U.S. and become citizens.

The OPT program is one of the primary attractions for international students choosing to study in the U.S..

Without OPT, most international students would be forced to leave the U.S. immediately after graduation, taking the skills they gained at American universities to foreign markets.

World.title: T.N. moves Supreme Court against HC striking down jobs to Karur stampede victims’ families
World.content:
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led Tamil Nadu government has moved the Supreme Court in appeal against a Madras High Court decision to strike down the grant of government jobs to the family members of Karur stampede victims.

The Madurai Bench of the High Court had quashed the government orders granting jobs to the victims’ family members on compassionate grounds on July 27.

The State had argued in the court that the appointments were meant as a humane gesture.

But the court concluded that specific guidelines covered the field of compassionate appointments, and they cannot be cast aside by the State government. The High Court had warned that the government’s action, if condoned, may run the risk of opening the floodgates.

Waiting list overlooked

The High Court had pointed out that there were wait-lists in every government department for appointments on compassionate grounds.

Employment has to be granted only in accordance with seniority and not with reference to the immediate nature of relief to be granted, the Division Bench of the High Court had noted.

The High Court had reasoned that it would be in violation of the fundamental rights of equality and due of process of law, enshrined in Article 14 and 21 of the Constitution, respectively, to overlook those in the waiting list in a bid to bring relief to the family members of the Karur stampede victims.

The State had contended that these jobs were given in exercise of its executive powers under Article 162 of the Constitution. But the High Court had responded that any exercise of executive authority of power had to be within the confines of the Constitution.

The stampede occurred in September last year during a TVK roadshow addressed by now Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay, who is also the party president.

World.title: Animal adoptions rise at Visakhapatnam zoo as families celebrate birthdays with wildlife
World.content:
On the morning of his birthday, instead of gifts, chocolates, and cakes, Sohan Gowtham Yenneti had something else in mind. A frequent visitor to Visakhapatnam’s Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (IGZP), he wanted his special day to include the animal he always stopped to admire. He ‘adopted’ a red-necked wallaby under the zoo’s animal adoption programme, adding his name to a steadily expanding list of citizens who are finding uncommon ways to support wildlife conservation.

His decision reflects a growing trend at the zoo over the past year. Symbolic animal adoption, once an occasional gesture by wildlife enthusiasts, is drawing increasing participation from families, school children, corporate organisations and individuals who wish to mark birthdays, anniversaries and other milestones with a contribution that extends beyond a single day. A symbolic adoption is a charitable donation rather than physically taking an animal home.

The numbers reflect that change. During the last financial year, IGZP recorded 80 animal adoptions, compared with 50 during the previous year, representing a 60% increase. Families continue to account for the largest share, with 72 family adoptions, while schools, colleges and corporate organisations are also beginning to participate with greater regularity. IGZP curator G Mangamma attributes the rise to a combination of sustained outreach and changing public attitudes towards wildlife. “People are gradually looking for meaningful ways to celebrate important occasions. Instead of spending on parties or gifts, many families are choosing to contribute towards the care of an animal. It gives children an opportunity to understand conservation in a very personal way,” she says.

A meaningful keepsake

The programme allows visitors to adopt an animal for a day, a month or a year by contributing towards its upkeep. The animal continues to remain under the care of the zoo, while the adopter receives an adoption certificate, complimentary entry benefits, a souvenir kit and, depending on the category, recognition at the enclosure. Contributions also qualify for income tax exemption under Section 80G.

Those opting for higher-value adoption categories receive complimentary entry to the zoo for multiple visits. These adopters also have their names displayed on a board outside the adopted animal’s enclosure. Additionally, some high-value category adopters enjoy unlimited zoo visits for a specified number of people during the adoption period. While these benefits acknowledge the adopter’s support, zoo officials emphasise that the lasting takeaway is a closer understanding of wildlife conservation.

The appeal cuts across age groups. While tigers, lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos and black panthers continue to attract considerable interest because of their popularity among visitors, several adopters are increasingly choosing reptiles, birds and lesser-known mammals. Macaws, peafowl, swans, crocodiles, snakes and tortoises also find enthusiastic supporters.

Mangamma believes that this widening preference is an encouraging sign. “We are particularly happy when visitors adopt species that usually receive less public attention. Every animal contributes to the ecological balance. When someone chooses a jackal, wild dog, crocodile or owl, it shows a deeper appreciation of biodiversity,” she says.

Many of the programme’s most memorable stories involve children. Parents increasingly report that the idea originates mostly with young visitors who form an attachment to a particular animal during repeated zoo visits. Some families now request relatives to contribute towards a ‘symbolic’ adoption instead of purchasing birthday presents.

“Children are often the strongest ambassadors for wildlife. We have seen them persuade parents to adopt their favourite animals. That emotional bond stays with them and encourages lasting concern for conservation,” Mangamma observes.

The educational value extends beyond symbolic adoption. During adoption events, zoo officials and keepers explain the adopted animal’s behaviour, diet, conservation status and daily care. Visitors leave with a better understanding of the responsibilities involved in maintaining healthy captive populations and protecting endangered species in the wild.

The programme has also found an unlikely champion within the zoo itself. Senior veterinarian Dr P Bhanu Babu has adopted the sarus crane, one of the world’s tallest flying birds and a species facing mounting pressures across its natural range.

A model gaining ground

IGZP is hardly alone in using public participation to strengthen conservation. Several Indian zoos have built thriving adoption programmes over the years. The Arignar Anna Zoological Park at Vandalur near Chennai regularly receives support from individuals and corporate organisations adopting large mammals. Mysuru Zoo remains one of the country’s most successful examples, where annual adoptions by industrial houses, philanthropists and families contribute substantially towards animal care.

Internationally, institutions such as the Taronga Zoo in Sydney and the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance have expanded the idea beyond local visitors. Their symbolic adoption programmes allow supporters from across the world to contribute towards conservation, research and habitat protection while receiving regular updates about the species they support. Although the scale differs, the underlying objective remains identical: creating a lasting relationship between people and wildlife.

Back in Visakhapatnam, IGZP plans to widen the programme through dedicated ‘Celebrate Your Birthday with Wildlife’ campaigns, anniversary and memorial adoption packages, school awareness initiatives and corporate adoption drives under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). The zoo also intends to strengthen its digital outreach, recognise repeat adopters and long-term conservation supporters and organise focused campaigns during Wildlife Week, World Environment Day and other occasions to encourage greater public participation in wildlife conservation.

(For details, visit the animal adoption section on vizagzoo.in).

World.title: BJP blames AAP govt in Punjab for ‘worsening drugs menace’
World.content:
Bharatiya Janata Party Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Thursday (July 30, 2026) blamed the Aam Aadmi Party government for the State’s, what he termed as “worsening drug crisis”, declaring that the AAP government’s widely-publicised ‘Yudh Nashian Virudh’ (War Against Drugs) campaign has failed entirely.

Mr. Dhillon said the AAP had during the 2022 poll campaign promised the people of Punjab that it would eradicate the drug menace within three months, after the party assumed power. “But today the situation has worsened instead of improving. Punjab’s youth are losing their lives every single day. When drug-affected families and ordinary citizens raise their voices against drug traffickers, they are openly threatened, which clearly indicates that the traffickers enjoy administrative and political patronage,” he alleged.

The BJP leader further said that public faith in the system has eroded to such an extent that families devastated by the drug menace are being forced to put up posters to sell their homes and stage protests.

“The increasing number of drug-related deaths and the growing public anger are clear evidence of the complete failure of the AAP government’s governance on this issue. The AAP government’s so-called promise of ‘change’ has come at a high cost for the people of Punjab and has pushed the state back by several years. The drug menace can be eradicated only through strong leadership and a robust policy framework, not through publicity campaigns and s,” he said, urging people of Punjab to elect a BJP government in the State in the upcoming assembly election, due in early 2027.

World.title: Mahila Manovikas eyes Guinness World Record with 13-km crochet tiranga bunting
World.content:
There is a certain rhythm to crochet that cannot be hurried. Every loop must find the next. Every knot must hold. Over the past few months, that rhythm has travelled from drawing rooms in Visakhapatnam to homes across India and overseas, where hundreds of hands have been working towards a common goal: knitting tricolour crochet flags for a World Record.

On August 1, more than 40,000 handmade crochet tricolour buntings stretching nearly 13 kilometres will be displayed at Port Stadium, Akkayyapalem, in what Mahila Manovikas hopes will become the world’s longest chain of crochet buntings and earn the organisation its fourth Guinness World Records title. A formal gathering of participants will follow on August 2 at CMR Function Hall, Venkojipalem.

The scale of the undertaking is striking. Around 330 crocheters, divided into six groups, have contributed to the project. They span generations, from school children and teenagers to Gen Z enthusiasts, homemakers, working professionals, senior citizens and experienced Guinness Record holders. Some learnt crochet only recently, while others have been practising the craft since childhood.

Founded in Visakhapatnam by Madhavi Suribhatla, Mahila Manovikas has steadily built a community around crochet while placing equal emphasis on women’s self-worth, skill-sharing and social engagement. The organisation’s earlier Guinness achievements include the display of 4,686 crochet caps in 2022, many of which were later donated to orphanages and old-age homes, followed by 2,719 handmade ponchos in 2023. The group had also undertaken large-scale crochet squares project, steadily widening both participation and ambition with every record attempt.

More than a record

For Madhavi, the record is only one part of a larger story.

“We have members from different countries and different walks of life. Many may never have met one another in person, but crochet has connected them through a common purpose,” she says. Crochet, Madhavi believes, offers participants much more than creative satisfaction. “Project Tiranga is about celebrating India’s identity while also showing how a traditional craft can continue to bring people together.”

One of the senior participants within the organisation is Nakka Padma, who has coordinated with participants both locally and from across cities and countries. Her own contribution to Project Tiranga stands at around 1,400 crochet flags.

“I began making the flags in April,” she says. “Every record pushes us to do better than the last. During our poncho record, I completed 70 ponchos. For the crochet squares project, my target was only 100, but I eventually made more than 3,000 squares. This time, I ended up making nearly 1,200.”

For Padma, the numbers represent persistence rather than competition. Each completed piece reflects evenings spent after household responsibilities, weekends devoted to crochet and countless hours shared with fellow members over calls and online groups.

Crafting an identity

Participants are travelling from several cities to attend the official ceremony. Among them is Anshu Malini from Bhubaneswar, who has been associated with Mahila Manovikas through four Guinness record attempts.

“I started learning crochet when I was eight years old,” she recalls. “My grandmother was the first teacher in our family. Craft was always valued at home.”

She is drawn to Mahila Manovikas because of its sense of community. “Every project teaches something new because people from different places contribute different ideas and techniques.” Crochet also reshaped how she sees herself. “When I began this journey, people knew me simply as someone’s daughter, wife or mother,” she says. “Crochet gave me an identity. Today, many people know me as ‘Guinness Malini’.”

Anshu describes herself as an “energy healer”, but says crochet has been equally therapeutic in her own life. “We started by crocheting for ourselves,” she says. “Later, Guinness records gave us recognition and a platform.”

Diversity remains one of Mahila Manovikas’ defining strengths. Unlike competitive craft circles, participation is measured less by expertise than by commitment. Beginners often work alongside seasoned crocheters who guide them through patterns, colour combinations and finishing techniques. The process becomes as valuable as the finished product.

The project has drawn first-time learners into a craft traditionally passed down generations. Among the youngest contributors is 10-year-old Anandita G K, who discovered crochet at a summer camp organised by Mahila Manovikas in association with Crafts Council of Andhra Pradesh earlier this year. Project Tiranga became her first large-scale assignment; weekends soon turned into crochet sessions as she patiently knitted tricolour flags alongside older participants.

“I had never crocheted before the summer camp, so making flags for this project was exciting,” she says. “Sometimes it was difficult to keep the stitches even, but I kept practising. I liked making something that will become part of a big display. Now, I want to learn more patterns.”

The organisation is also looking beyond record books to include charitable distribution, while members are exploring ways to introduce handcrafted crochet products into mainstream retail spaces.

World.title: One killed after building collapses in Bhiwandi; at least seven trapped under rubble
World.content:
The death toll in the Bhiwandi building collapse in Maharashtra’s Thane district rose to six early on Friday (July 31, 2026) morning, after rescuers recovered another body from the debris of a partially collapsed four-storey building.

The four-storey building partially collapsed late on Thursday (July 30, 2026) night in Bhiwandi, triggering a large-scale rescue operation involving the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).

Officials are yet to ascertain the exact cause of the collapse, and further details are awaited.

Authorities have not yet confirmed the number of people who were inside the building at the time of the incident.

The structure comprised 48 rooms, 12 on each floor, municipal officials said. The building had been declared dangerous by the civic body. Tragedy struck while repair work was underway on the premises.

Around 9 p.m. on Thursday (July 30), residents heard “loud cracking sounds” emanating from the structure, an official said.

Fearing the worst, locals immediately helped evacuate many families to other locations. However, while some occupants were still making their way out, the ‘B’ wing of the building caved in, he said.

A major multi-agency rescue operation is underway, comprising teams from the National Disaster Response Force, Thane Disaster Response Force and local fire brigade. A dog squad, four fire engines, two ambulances, and heavy earth-moving machinery has been deployed at the site.

(With inputs from ANI, PTI)

World.title: Tirupati all set for Thyagaraja music festival from August 1

TTD’s Executive Officer M. Ravichandra, who is also the ex-officio president of the festival committee, will formally unveil the portrait of late M. Krishnaswami, the former chairman of the cultural trust as part of his centenary celebrations on August 1. Former Chief Election Commissioner T.S. World.title: ‘Dare to demand Modi’s resignation?’: Student part of NEET protest alleges assault in Bengaluru
World.content:
A 19-year-old student associated with the All India Students’ Association (AISA) was allegedly assaulted by four unidentified men in Bengaluru’s Jalahalli area on July 28, with the students’ organisation alleging that the attackers were “suspected goons” affiliated with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).

The police said they have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against unknown persons. “We are investigating the case, and efforts are on to identify and trace the four accused. No arrests have been made so far,” a police officer said.

World.title: Spider-Man Brand New Day surpasses Pathaan, Kantara Chapter 1; earns Rs 72 crore in India
World.content:
Spider-Man Brand New Day Box Office Collection Day 1: Proving that Spider-Man is a superhero not just on screen but also at the box office, director Destin Daniel Cretton’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day, starring Tom Holland and Zendaya in the lead roles, registered a thunderous opening in India, grossing over Rs 72 crore. In fact, the movie has outperformed Siddharth Anand’s Shah Rukh Khan-Deepika Padukone starrer Pathaan (2023) and Aditya Dhar’s Ranveer Singh-led Dhurandhar (2025) on its debut day.

Moreover, Spider-Man: Brand New Day also recorded the highest opening day collection for a Hollywood movie in India, thus scripting history. On Thursday, July 30, the superhero film grossed Rs 72.44 crore in India, according to industry tracker Sacnilk.

Check Out | Jana Nayagan Box Office Collection Day 8 Updates: Vijay’s film crosses Rs 260 crore mark worldwide

Spider-Man Brand New Day scripts history with biggest Hollywood opening in India

During the day, the film recorded an India nett collection of Rs 60.60 crore. Thus, it surpassed the previous records set by the Russo brothers’ 2019 epic Avengers: Endgame (Rs 65 crore gross; Rs 53.60 crore nett) and James Cameron’s 2022 film Avatar: The Way of Water (Rs 48.75 crore gross; Rs 40.30 crore nett).

Spider-Man: Brand New Day also fared better than Pathaan and Kantara Chapter 1, which grossed Rs 67.19 crore and Rs 73.29 crore, respectively, on their opening days. Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Animal earned Rs 76.10 crore in India on opening day. It must be noted that the MCU film did not have any block bookings.



During the day, the superhero film witnessed an overall occupancy rate of 56.58 per cent in the country. While the morning shows commenced with 51.22 per cent occupancy, the rate remained unchanged during the afternoon screenings, before soaring to 58.78 per cent in the evening and 65.11 per cent at night.

Spider-Man Brand New Day worldwide box office collection

If it maintains the same momentum in the coming days, Spider-Man: Brand New Day could easily become the highest-grossing Hollywood film in India soon, surpassing Avatar: The Way of Water’s Rs 477.50 crore and Avengers: Endgame’s Rs 445 crore. According to early estimates by Sacnilk, the movie has grossed over Rs 1,000 crore worldwide thus far. In the US, the film is releasing a day after India, on July 31.

Also starring Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Florence Pugh, Tramell Tillman, Marisa Tomei, and Mark Ruffalo in key roles, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a sequel to Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017), Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019), and Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021). While the earlier three films were helmed by Jon Watts, he was replaced by Destin Daniel Cretton this time. This is the 38th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session 2026 Day 10 LIVE: Bill to increase Supreme Court judges likely to be discussed in Lok Sabha today
World.content:
Rajya Sabha proceedings are underway during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi on Thursday. (Sansad TV/ANI Video Grab)

Bills to be taken up today: Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal is likely to take up the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, for consideration in the Lok Sabha. Home Minister Amit Shah will move the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, while Parliament will also take up the Joint Committee’s report on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, and the Government of Union Territories (Amendment) Bill, 2025.

Paper Leak Bill passed in both Houses: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, has been passed in both the Houses of the Parliament. The Rajya Sabha passed it on Thursday night by voice vote after the Lok Sabha cleared it a day earlier, amid an Opposition walkout. The amended Bill prescribes a jail term of 5 to 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh for those involved in paper leaks or exam malpractice. For organised paper leak rackets, the bill provides a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. The amended anti-paper leak law empowers states and Union Territories to designate Sessions Courts as special fast-track courts to hear offences under the Act. It also mandates day-to-day hearings and aims to complete trials within three months of the filing of the charge sheet.

World.title: Anthropic says Claude AI models breached systems of 3 companies during cybersecurity tests
World.content:
Amid the intensifying debate around autonomous AI systems and cybersecurity, frontier AI lab Anthropic, on Thursday, July 30, said that it had found three separate incidents where its Claude AI models gained access to the real systems of three organisations.

The Dario Amodei-led company said that these discoveries were made during a large-scale retrospective review of its cybersecurity evaluations. The company admitted that the latest review was triggered by a similar security incident that was revealed by OpenAI last week.

In a blog post, Anthropic detailed the security incidents, admitting that its Claude AI models had accidentally accessed real-world computer systems during cybersecurity evaluations. According to the company, the incidents were the result of a misconfigured testing environment rather than the AI intentionally trying to escape or attack real organisations.

Anthropic’s disclosure comes amid growing concerns over AI’s increasingly advanced cybersecurity capabilities. The incidents involved three Claude models, Opus 4.7, Mythos 5 and an internal research model, which reacted differently after encountering real-world systems. While Opus 4.7 continued its attack and Mythos 5 mistakenly believed it was still in a simulation, the research model stopped once it recognised the target was real.

Anthropic said the models were being tested without the additional safeguards used in public releases. The company has paused all cyber evaluations, and is investigating the incidents with independent AI evaluator METR, and has urged other AI labs to conduct similar reviews.

What happened?

The incidents emerged after OpenAI recently revealed that its flagship AI models had escaped a test environment by exploiting a software vulnerability and eventually breaching the infrastructure of Hugging Face. Meanwhile, in its response, Anthropic said that it reviewed over 141,000 cybersecurity evaluation runs and spotted three cases where Claude had internet access when it was supposed to be isolated.

According to the company, the AI models were participating in “capture-the-flag” exercises, which is part of common cybersecurity challenges where they are directed to break into fictional systems to find hidden information. The Claude AI models had been explicitly told that it had no internet access and that everything it encountered was part of a simulation. However, the company said that due to a configuration mistake, the testing systems were actually connected to the internet. Consequently, when Claude found real websites and servers, it mistakenly believed they were part of the exercise.



In the first case, Claude attacked the infrastructure of a real company after confusing it with the fictional target in the exercise. The AI exploited weak passwords and exposed services to gain access to production data. In the second instance, Claude created and uploaded a malicious Python package to the public PyPI software repository as it believed this would help it to accomplish the challenge. According to Anthropic’s findings, the package stayed online for about an hour before being removed. It was downloaded by numerous real systems, including one belonging to a security company.

Meanwhile, in the third incident, an internal research model scanned thousands of internet-connected systems and compromised one company by deploying common hacking techniques. Anthropic said that when the model realised that the target was a real organisation, it stopped the attack on its own.

Further, Anthropic said that there is no evidence that Claude tried to escape its test environment, steal itself, or pursue its own goals. Instead, the models believed they were following the instructions of the cybersecurity exercise. The company also notes that the models involved were running without the additional safeguards that are normally included in publicly available versions of Claude.

Following the incidents, Anthropic halted its cybersecurity evaluations, informed the affected organisations, and claimed that it has been strengthening its testing procedures since. The company plans to improve monitoring, tighten security around evaluation environments, and work more closely with external testing partners to prevent similar mistakes in the future.



Cybersecurity capabilities of advanced AI models

So far, July has seen a series of incidents that have heightened concerns about the cyber capabilities of advanced AI models. The most significant came on July 21, when OpenAI disclosed that one of its pre-release AI agents escaped an isolated testing environment by exploiting a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability and breached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure during a cybersecurity evaluation. The incident prompted OpenAI to tighten testing controls and collaborate with Hugging Face on new safeguards.

Anthropic’s disclosure followed after it reviewed more than 141,000 cybersecurity evaluation runs and found three separate cases where Claude models accessed real-world systems after a testing environment had been mistakenly left connected to the internet. Unlike the OpenAI case, Anthropic said its models did not exploit novel vulnerabilities; instead, they relied on basic techniques such as weak passwords and exposed endpoints.

Cybersecurity experts say the two incidents highlight that the biggest risk today lies not only in increasingly capable AI models, but also in inadequately secured testing environments. The disclosures have renewed calls for stronger sandboxing, continuous monitoring and industry-wide standards for evaluating advanced AI systems before deployment.

World.title: 4 dead, several trapped after residential building collapses near Mumbai

Rescue workers at the spot of the building collapse in Bhiwandi (Express Photo by Deepak Joshi).
